extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), unit commanders, unit public affairs representatives (UPARs), and Army civilians responsible for public communication and releases
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and criteria for preparing, clearing, and releasing official Army public affairs products (news releases, web content, social media, imagery, and community outreach communications). Covers authority, ethics, OPSEC/privacy protections, synchronization, and publication/records requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Be truthful at all times. PA Soldiers and civilians will hold themselves to be key experts in their craft, ensuring all information for release is accurate, truthful, timely, and presented in its proper context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA personnel must verify facts before release; presenting information in proper context is required. This is an explicit professional-ethics requirement (1–11 f (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum disclosure, minimum delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide unclassified information about the Army and its activities to the public with maximum disclosure and minimum delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the most information available for release in the shortest time allowable (1–11 f (4); commanders 2–4a(4)). Must balance disclosure with OPSEC, safety, privacy and legal constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSEC and pre-release review
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAO conducts an OPSEC review of all official information before it is released to the public. Examples of products requiring automatic review include: news releases; web content; teaching, speaking, and writing done by military personnel pertaining to military and national security matters in an unofficial capacity; subjects of significant concern to DoD; and responses to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must be OPSEC level II qualified. OPSEC review is mandatory to prevent release of information that could endanger forces or operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of classified and controlled unclassified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not release information that would adversely affect national security; protect classified information and controlled unclassified information in the interest of national security under AR 380 – 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All releases must be checked against classification and CUI policies. If in doubt, coordinate with security/ops/legal authorities before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and PII safeguarding
rubrics_metrics.description: There are stringent restrictions for protecting personally identifiable information (PII). The Privacy Act of 1974 prevents the release of certain personal information to the public. There are strict reporting requirements if PII is released, even inadvertently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Privacy Act/PII rules before publishing names, medical or other personal details; follow Appendix D (Guidance on Release of Information under the Privacy Act) and reporting procedures for inadvertent disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to release / designated spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: PA is an inherently governmental function; official spokespersons must be military, DoD, or Army civilian employees. The CPA will ensure all necessary staff coordination and clearance have been completed prior to releasing information outside the Department of the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only authorized officials may make official statements. Units must designate spokespersons; clearances must be obtained through command channels and CPA as required (2–1, 2–2, glossary: Official statement/Spokesperson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearance of information: Approval by the reviewing authority to publish or release submitted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submitted material must receive appropriate reviewing authority approval before publication; UPAR products are subject to normal PA editing and release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial and objective dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartial and objective dissemination (chapter 7 — public communication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs releases should be factual, objective, and nonpartisan; avoid promotional or partisan messaging. Maintain credibility to the widest audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Countering misinformation and disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: PA can mitigate and counter adversary disinformation and misinformation with accurate and timely public information and imagery, consistent with DoD PA guidance, PA ethics, OPSEC, information security, safety, and privacy of DoD personnel and their Families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counter-messaging must preserve credibility and adhere to OPSEC and privacy constraints; PA programs should be proactive and maintain relationships with media (1–13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander’s communication synchronization (CCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCS is the process for coordinating and synchronizing themes, messages, images, operations, and actions to support U.S. Government strategic communication-related objectives and ensure the integrity and consistency of themes and messages to the lowest tactical level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CCS to plan, develop, and execute goal-based communication plans; PAO leads CCS at unit level to align with DA themes and broader national strategic narrative (1–12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely release and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for information from organizations and private citizens should be answered quickly. The commander is responsible to disseminate accurate and timely information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must respond expeditiously to media and public requests; delays must be justified and minimized. Timeliness also supports countering misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unfavorable news
rubrics_metrics.description: Release unfavorable news with the same care and speed as favorable news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suppress negative information to protect image; transparency increases credibility. Coordinate with legal/operational authorities as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on staged publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Not engage in releases, events, or activities staged solely for self-serving or promotional publicity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs support must not be used for selective benefit or commercial/political gain; evaluate requests against selective benefit and appropriateness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial control and UPAR oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: UPAR products are subject to normal PA editing and release procedures. PAOs are responsible for cultivating, coordinating, and training UPARs; UPARs operate under the oversight of the higher echelon PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unit-generated content must be checked/edited by PA professionals prior to release; UPARs require certification and follow ALMS training courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The records management requirement for all record numbers, associated forms, and reports required by this publication are addressed in the Records Retention Schedule-Army (RRS – A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of releases and related documentation per ARIMS/RRS-A and DA Pam 25–403 guidance; ensure traceability for FOIA/privacy/legal needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with professional codes of ethics and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: PA Soldiers and civilians should be familiar with industry best practices and codes of ethics as published by the International Association of Business Communicators, the Public Relations Society of America, and the Arthur W. Page Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt relevant professional standards to inform release practices and ethical decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers, enlisted Soldiers, and civilians working and supervising PA offices will qualify through the appropriate level of the Defense Information School training. Non-PA staff sections or officials will not be assigned primary responsibility for planning, directing, or executing PA missions. All career program 22 (CP22) civilian PA managing and supervising PA offices will meet OPM qualification standards and complete CP22 training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure personnel releasing information have required training/credentials (Defense Information School, CP22), and the PAO is directly rated by the commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution rules and background briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: Background: Remarks that may be reported only if attributed to a nonspecific source such as an Army official. A background discussion or briefing may be held to give news media representatives a better understanding of a situation. This form of attribution must be agreed upon in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background briefings require prior agreement on attribution; cameras cannot be used. Records of background briefings are not exempt from FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official vs unofficial digital presence
rubrics_metrics.description: External official presence: Any Army PA office websites, installation and unit websites, or official social media outlets used to interact with the audience on behalf of a command. Digital media: Army PA content that is released on a website, blog, or social media platform will fall into this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate official accounts (subject to PA policy, editorial control, records retention) from personal or nonaccredited accounts; follow chapter 8 guidance on social media, nonaccredited accounts, and personal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website and content management standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate with CIO/G‑6 to provide oversight and control of the content on Army public websites as the official primary point of access to Army information on the internet. The CPA will manage Army public website policy and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official webpages must follow organizational website publishing guidance, publication guidelines, and content-management platform rules (8–7, 8–8, 8–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarded information and legal constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PA releases must be consistent with OPSEC, information security, safety, and privacy of DoD personnel and their Families; safeguarded information requires protection under AR 380–5 or other controlling guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with legal, security, and OPSEC officers prior to release if content may contain safeguarded or legally protected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling information during criminal investigations and crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates procedures to avoid the release of critical information during ongoing criminal investigations and crisis communication (summary changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During investigations/crises coordinate with appropriate authorities (CID, legal, operational leads) to avoid jeopardizing investigations or safety; follow chapter 7 (crisis communication) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of imagery and visual information policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish public affairs policy guidance for release of Army visual information (VI) products to the public; VI planning and archiving requirements exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow VI policy for photographing/recording personnel—especially in hostile areas—archive VI per guidance, and ensure imagery does not reveal sensitive positions or PII (3–3, 3–4, 2–2 a(11), glossary entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of PA support and selective benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid providing selective benefit. Appropriate public affairs support is that PA support the responsible PAO and their commander decides is suitable to meet a PA requirement of a unit within the installation’s local area of PA responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate requests for PA support against criteria such as public interest, mutual benefit, incidental vs essential support, and selective benefit prohibitions; consider cost-sharing and Army share of costs guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority/waiver and higher-level coordination for special events (e.g., aerial demonstrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DCS, G‑3/5/7 is the exception and waiver authority for requests for Army aerial demonstrations for public affairs missions and may waive submission requirements for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special events like aerial demos have specific submission timelines (e.g., 40-day/60-day) and approval authorities; coordinate early with appropriate approving authorities and CPA.
